title: Restriction transport at a geometric point: coefficient normalization and derived naturality
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], not necessarily one over $k_0$. Use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse image $G=g^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ or $\mathcal O_E$, use the finite constant or completed coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the structure isomorphism $c_\Lambda:G\Lambda_s\to\Lambda_s$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. The action on $GM$ is transported by $c_\Lambda^{-1}$.

Write $U=(s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}s)$ and $V=(s\xrightarrow g s)$. For a sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda_s$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}:M(V)\to(GM)(U)$ be the coprojection at $(V,(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}):U\to u_g(V))$ into the inverse-image colimit of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], followed by sheafification. Define $\sigma^g_M=\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}\operatorname{res}_g:M(U)\to(GM)(U)$. Under the natural evaluation identification $(GM)(U)\cong M(V)$ of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}$ is the identity, so $\sigma^g_M$ identifies with restriction along $g:V\to U$. For a constant section $b\in\Lambda$ one has $\sigma^g_{\Lambda_s}(b)=c_\Lambda^{-1}(b)$, and $\sigma^g_M(bx)=c_\Lambda^{-1}(b)\sigma^g_M(x)$.

Termwise on any unbounded complex $N$, these maps form a $\Lambda$-linear chain map $\sigma^g_N:\Gamma(s,N)\to\Gamma(s,GN)$, natural in chain maps. Here both module actions use constant sections and the target uses $c_\Lambda^{-1}$. For every derived morphism $v:N\to N'$ in $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the induced maps satisfy $\Gamma(s,Gv)\sigma^g_N=\sigma^g_{N'}\Gamma(s,v)$; thus they define a natural transformation on the entire derived category. The sections functor is that of [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]; no constructibility, boundedness or derived-completeness hypothesis on $N$ is imposed.

proof.text: Compute the distinguished coprojection before sheafification. For every site object $T=(T\xrightarrow t s)$, use [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (1) to form the site object $B_T=(T\xrightarrow{g\circ t}s)$ and let $\beta_T:T\to u_g(B_T)$ have projections $(t,\mathrm{id}_T)$. This is defined since both composites to the target $s$ are $g\circ t$. For an index $(W,\phi:T\to u_g(W))$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], let $a:T\to W$ be the second projection of $\phi$. The fibre-product equation is $w\circ a=g\circ t$, so $a:B_T\to W$ is a site morphism and $u_g(a)\beta_T=\phi$. Conversely that equality forces $a$ to be this projection. Thus $(B_T,\beta_T)$ is initial in $\mathcal I_T$, hence terminal in $\mathcal I_T^{\mathrm{op}}$. For any sheaf $F$, the restrictions $F(W)\to F(B_T)$ form a colimit cocone: a cocone is determined by its component at this terminal index, and every other component is its composite with the restriction just displayed. Consequently the coprojection $F(B_T)\to(u_{g,p}F)(T)$ is invertible, with inverse sending the coprojection of $x\in F(W)$ to $F(a)(x)$. These formulas commute with maps of sheaves and with restrictions in $T$.

source.place: Tag 00VE, lemma-adjoints-u, preceding definition of the index category and colimit; explicit initial-index calculation for an isomorphism g (agent).

proof.text: The presheaf just computed is $T\mapsto F(B_T)=F(\Phi_gT)$. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (1), $\Phi_g$ is an equivalence preserving coverings in both directions. In particular it preserves the fibre products of a covering family, so the sheaf equalizer condition for this presheaf is exactly that for $F$ on the image covering; hence it is already a sheaf. Its sheafification map is therefore an isomorphism: by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], the identity map to this sheaf extends to an inverse, and uniqueness makes both composites identities. We have thus obtained the natural evaluation identification of that inverse-image lemma using the actual coprojections, with the distinguished coprojection equal to the identity in these coordinates. For $T=U$, $B_T=V$ and $\beta_T=(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$. Hence the map $\sigma^g_M=\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}\operatorname{res}_g$ in the statement identifies precisely with the restriction $M(g):M(U)\to M(V)$, not an unspecified isomorphism of those section modules.

proof.text: At finite level write $A=A_{E,n}$. A constant section $b$ restricts to the same constant $b$ on $V$, since all restrictions of the constant presheaf are identities [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The structure map is the adjoint of $\rho_A^g:A_s\to g_*A_s$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] is the colimit adjunction followed by sheafification. Explicitly, its adjoint at the coprojection indexed by $(W,\phi:T\to u_g(W))$ sends $x\in A_s(W)$ to $A_s(\phi)(\rho_{A,W}^g(x))$: these maps are a cocone because restrictions commute with $\rho_A^g$, and sheafification extends this cocone uniquely. For the distinguished index $(V,\beta_U)$ and a constant $b$, $\rho_{A,V}^g(b)$ is constant $b$ on $u_g(V)$ by its definition, and restriction along $\beta_U$ is constant $b$ on $U$. Therefore $c_A\sigma^g_{A_s}(b)=b$. Since $c_A$ is invertible by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (3), $\sigma^g_{A_s}(b)=c_A^{-1}(b)$.

proof.text: For integral coefficients put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ with projections $\pi_m:R\to(A_{E,m})_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For $b\in\mathcal O_E$, its constant section is the compatible family of constants $b_m=b\bmod\varpi_E^m$. Naturality of restriction and of the coprojections, proved above, gives $(G\pi_m)\sigma^g_R(b)=\sigma^g_{(A_{E,m})_s}(b_m)$. The structure isomorphism of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] satisfies $\pi_m c_{\mathcal O_E}=c_{A_{E,m}}G\pi_m$. Hence, by the finite-level calculation, $\pi_m c_{\mathcal O_E}\sigma^g_R(b)=c_{A_{E,m}}\sigma^g_{(A_{E,m})_s}(b_m)=b_m=\pi_m(b)$ for every $m$. Sections of the limit are compatible families, so their projections are jointly injective [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. It follows that $c_{\mathcal O_E}\sigma^g_R(b)=b$, and invertibility of $c_{\mathcal O_E}$ gives $\sigma^g_R(b)=c_{\mathcal O_E}^{-1}(b)$. This compares sections of the completed sheaf itself; no identification with the discrete constant sheaf $\mathcal O_E$ is used.

source.place: Tags 03CO, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves (2), and 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; the completed structure map is the one defined in def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison.

proof.text: For either coefficient sheaf $R=\Lambda_s$, restriction in a sheaf of modules obeys $\operatorname{res}_g(ax)=\operatorname{res}_g(a)\operatorname{res}_g(x)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The inverse image carries the action map $R\times M\to M$ to $GR\times GM\to GM$ using its finite-product comparison [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. In the evaluation coordinates computed in steps 1-2 these are precisely the original ring and module operations on $R(V)$ and $M(V)$: apply naturality of those coordinates to the action, addition and zero maps; the product comparison is coordinatewise. Thus $\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}(a_Vx_V)=\operatorname{ins}_{g,R}(a_V)\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}(x_V)$. Combining the two displayed identities yields $\sigma^g_M(ax)=\sigma^g_R(a)\sigma^g_M(x)$. For a constant $a=b\in\Lambda$, steps 3-4 identify $\sigma^g_R(b)$ with $c_\Lambda^{-1}(b)$. The target's $\Lambda_s$-action is exactly multiplication by $c_\Lambda^{-1}$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Therefore this semilinearity identity is $\Lambda$-linearity for the actions in the statement. Additivity follows in the same coordinates from additivity of restriction and of the inverse-image coprojection.

proof.text: Let $f:M\to M'$ be a module-sheaf morphism. Its presheaf naturality gives $f_V\operatorname{res}_g=\operatorname{res}_g f_U$, and functoriality of the colimit and sheafification gives $(Gf)_U\operatorname{ins}_{g,M}=\operatorname{ins}_{g,M'}f_V$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Multiplication of these equations gives $(Gf)_U\sigma^g_M=\sigma^g_{M'}f_U$. Apply this first to each differential $d^i:N^i\to N^{i+1}$. The resulting identity says that the maps $\sigma^g_{N^i}$ are a chain map between the two termwise section complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; step 5 gives its $\Lambda$-linearity in every degree. Apply the same identity to each component of any chain map $N\to N'$ to obtain naturality on complexes. The argument is degreewise for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, so it applies to unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tag 00VE, lemma-adjoints-u (bifunctorial colimit adjunction), and Tag 06UM, section-pullback; derived.tex Tag 05RU, definition-derived-category. Explicit degreewise naturality calculation (agent).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], sections at $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ are exact on modules over every ring sheaf, preserve quasi-isomorphisms termwise and induce the stated functor on the entire unbounded derived category; its field hypothesis holds since $k$ in the item is algebraically closed. Regarding these section modules as $\Lambda$-modules through constant sections changes neither kernels nor images, so it also preserves quasi-isomorphisms with values in $D(\Lambda)$. The transported module inverse image $G$ is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms also for completed coefficients, as stated in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Let $Q_s$ and $Q_\Lambda$ be the localization functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus both complex functors $F=Q_\Lambda\Gamma(s,-)$ and $H=Q_\Lambda\Gamma(s,G(-))$ invert all quasi-isomorphisms. Step 6 gives a natural transformation $F\to H$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) to $L=Q_s$, $W$ the quasi-isomorphisms and target category $D(\Lambda)$: this transformation descends uniquely to the two indicated derived functors with components the classes of $\sigma^g_N$. Its naturality for every derived morphism $v:N\to N'$ is exactly $\Gamma(s,Gv)\sigma^g_N=\sigma^g_{N'}\Gamma(s,v)$. The cited localization statement imposes no boundedness, constructibility or completeness assumption, and neither do the two exact functors used here.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q91-23e6342ea (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 7 steps, and the statement of every node it cites. The statement and its 11 stmt_deps are unchanged and there are no new nodes. The live and side-live copies are still unsplit, so nothing supersedes it; there is no cycle (the item is not in the closure of its deps) and no SGA citation. Steps 1-2: I_T has the initial index (B_T=(T,g∘t), β_T=(t,id)) and the unique arrow is the second projection. The presheaf F∘Φ_g is a sheaf because Φ_g is a covering-preserving equivalence (lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image (1)); the inverse to sheafification follows from the universal property. So σ is restriction along g:V→U. Step 3: c_A=ε∘G(ρ) with the explicit 00VE counit, which I checked at sites.tex lines 594-607; this gives c_Aσ(b)=b, and lemma (3) gives invertibility. Step 4 uses π_m c_O = c_{A_m}G(π_m) and invertibility from def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, plus sectionwise limits from def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit; the completed sheaf is used throughout, not a discrete constant sheaf. Steps 5-6 are elementary semilinearity, chain-map and naturality computations, degreewise for unbounded complexes. Step 7: sections are exact at an algebraically closed k, G is exact on transported completed modules (comparison definition), and the transformation descends by localization-universal-property leaf clause (2). Hypotheses check out: ℓ≠p makes ℓ invertible on s, k is algebraically closed, and nothing assumes g fixes k_0. I accept the three declared tool_uses (two generic sk-def-sf-admissible lemmas and one Mathlib adjunction leaf). The citer lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural uses the item for its clause 1 unchanged. Advisory, not a fault: the statement attributes 'the natural evaluation identification' to the iso lemma, whose statement only asserts that some natural iso exists; step 2 constructs the explicit one.
